s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral weakness and neurological deficits following a sudden pain episode, with a history of cardiovascular disease
salient_findings: Left arm and left leg weakness
Tingling in the left arm and left leg
Intraluminal clot in the thoracic aorta
Multiple acute embolic infarcts on brain MRI
key_facts: 53-year-old man
History of hypertension
History of hyperlipidemia
History of diabetes mellitus type 2
History of heart failure with recovered ejection fraction
Previous hospitalization for cardiac issues
Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed an ejection fraction of 30% with global hypokinesis
Underwent CABG with Impella 5.5 support
Discharged home on postoperative day 7
Symptoms began 90 minutes before presentation
Sneezing preceded pain throughout the head
Pain was followed by tingling and weakness in the left arm and left leg
Blood pressure: 146/85 mm Hg
Heart rate: 87 beats/min
Oxygen saturation: 97% on room air
Respiratory rate: 18 breaths/min
National Institute of Health Stroke Scale score was 2
CT scan of head and CT angiography of head and neck were negative for acute findings
CT angiography of chest revealed an intraluminal clot in the thoracic aorta
MRI of brain showed multiple acute embolic infarcts

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial weakness with bilateral lower motor neuron involvement in a patient with a history of chemotherapy

Inability to close her eyelids
Difficulty raising her eyebrows
Bilateral lower motor neuron facial muscle weakness
key_facts: 56-year-old woman
Locally advanced, unresectable pancreatic adenocarcinoma
Received four cycles of Folfirinox chemotherapy without significant response
Received gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel therapy
Developed bilateral facial drooping after 20 cycles of combined therapy and 16 additional cycles of nab-paclitaxel alone

Developed severe edema due to capillary leak which led to discontinuation of gemcitabine
Neurological evaluation revealed bilateral lower motor neuron facial muscle weakness
MRI Brain revealed bilateral facial nerve enhancement compatible with bilateral facial neuritis

Midnight salivary cortisol was elevated on two consecutive nights
Histological examination showed stage T2N2B disease with lymphovascular and perineural invasion
Immunohistochemical staining was positive for ACTH in 30-40% of invasive tumor cells

salient_findings: Shortness of breath and hypoxia
Facial and nasal swelling
Black eschar on the nasal root
Pansinusitis
Bilateral lung infiltrations
Presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa
key_facts: Patient is a 67-year-old male
Patient has uncontrolled diabetes
Patient had COVID-19 infection at the end of December 2022
Patient was admitted to hospital on January 1st, 2023
Patient developed new symptoms on January 11th, including nasal ache, dyspnea, and facial and nasal swelling
Initial examination showed temperature of 36.5°C, heart rate of 116, respiratory rate of 26, blood pressure of 150/88 mmHg, and O2 saturation of 90% in room air
Laboratory tests showed white blood cell count of 2 × 10^9/L, creatinine of 178 umol/L, blood sugar of 11.6 mmol/L, and platelet count of 17 × 10^9/L
Imaging studies showed pansinusitis, bilateral lung infiltrations, and presence of fungal hyphae and spores in nasal mucosa
Blood metagenomics next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected Rhizopus microsporum and Mucor racemosus

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute febrile illness with multi-organ involvement and epidemic potential
salient_findings: Fever, headache, sore throat, and general discomfort
Leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, and elevated liver enzymes
Bilateral pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, and liver edema
key_facts: 42-year-old male with no prior health problems
Living in an HFRS epidemic area
Not vaccinated
Developed symptoms six days before admission
Initial body temperature: 36.5°C
Pulse rate: 86 beats per minute
Respiratory rate: 18 beats per minute
Blood pressure: 118/77 mmHg
Slight flushing of the face
Leukocytosis present
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and alpha hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase (α-HBDH)
Thrombocytopenia
Elevated urea, uric acid, and creatine levels
Declining levels of lymphocytes, CD8+ T cells, and NK cells
Positive serological test for HTNV immunoglobulin M (IgM) and IgG
Positive COVID-19 nasal and throat swabs

s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory illness with fever and pulmonary infiltrates
salient_findings: Cough and sputum with intermittent fever for 3 days
Highest temperature reached 41°C with chills
Multiple patchy high-density shadows in both lungs on chest X-ray and CT
Elevated white blood cell count with neutrophilia
key_facts: 62-year-old male patient
Past medical history of tuberculosis 10 years ago
Recent poor sleep (2-3 hours per day)
Temperature 40.2°C on admission
Few wet rales audible on lung auscultation
White blood cell count: 11.24 × 10^9/L with 80.7% neutrophils
Lymphocyte count: 1.08 × 10^9/L
Serum albumin: 29.3 g/L
Ferritin: 450.91 ng/mL
C-reactive protein: 28.3 mg/L
Blood sedimentation rate: 57 mm/hr

Normal results for routine urine/stool exam, calcitonin gene, coagulation function, HIV antibody, β-D-glucan, galactomannan, respiratory pathogen nucleic acid, lung tumor markers, T lymphocyte subpopulation, T-spot test
